# Code of Conduct

Netrune is built by and for people who keep networks running. Everyone is
welcome here, whatever their experience, background, or the size of their
network: a first-time contributor fixing a typo matters as much as a
long-time maintainer.

## What we expect

- Be kind and patient, especially with newcomers and questions that seem basic.
- Assume good intent; ask before concluding.
- Critique ideas and code, never people.
- Accept that a "no" or "not yet" on a proposal is about the project's scope
  and safety rules, not about you.
- Credit others' work, and say so when you are unsure.

## What we do not accept

- Harassment, insults, or demeaning comments of any kind.
- Discrimination based on identity, background, or experience.
- Publishing anyone's private information, including their network details.
- Sustained disruption of discussions, issues, or reviews.

## Reporting

If someone's behaviour makes you uncomfortable, tell the maintainers
privately: open a private report on this repository (**Security → Report a
vulnerability** reaches only the maintainers), and say it is a conduct
report. Reports are handled confidentially. Maintainers may edit or remove
comments, close threads, or ban participants who break this code, starting
with a private warning where that is enough.

This code applies in the repository, its issues, pull requests, and
discussions, and anywhere someone represents the project.

Adapted from the [Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/), version 2.1.
